source_evidence: A frequent mistake people make is putting money they will not need for a very long time in investments that pay a low amount of interest.
question: Misconception: Money I won’t need for many years should always be kept in low-interest investments because they are the safest choice.
answer: Your time horizon matters. The source says putting money you will not need for a very long time in low-interest investments can be a mistake, since it may grow too slowly. For a short-term goal of five years or less, it cautions against risky investments because you may have to sell at a loss when the money is needed.
